title: $\RHom$ preserves bounded constructible complexes ($\ell$-adic $\Lambda$)
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be one of $\underline{\cO}_E$, $\underline E$ ($E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite;
[sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]) or $\underline{\Qlb}$ ([sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]), and let $X$
be a scheme of the setting of [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. If $K,L\in D(\Mod_{\Lambda_X})$ are bounded
constructible ([sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible]), then so is $\RHom_{\Lambda_X}(K,L)$
([sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom]).

external.place: Since $K$ is bounded constructible, reduction modulo $\varpi$ gives $$ \RHom(K,L)/\varpi\cong\RHom_{\cO_E/\varpi}(K/\varpi,L/\varpi). $$ By Deligne's finiteness theorem for the internal $\RHom$ (SGA 4½, *Th. finitude*, 1.6) on the finite type $k$-scheme $X$, with coefficients in which $p$ is invertible, this is a bounded complex with constructible cohomology.

The cases $\underline E$ and $\underline{\Qlb}$ follow by inverting $\ell$ and by descending to a finite extension $E$ ([sk-thm-sfb-qlbar-two-colimit]), as in [lem-sfb-dc-lower-star-preserves]; see Bhatt–Scholze, §6.8.

The cases $\underline E$ and $\underline{\Qlb}$ follow by inverting $\ell$ and by descending to a finite extension $E$ ([sk-thm-sfb-qlbar-two-colimit]), as in [lem-sfb-dc-lower-star-preserves]; see Bhatt–Scholze, §6.8.

proof.text: First consider $\Lambda=\underline{\mathcal O_E}$. The only ideals of $k$ are $0$ and $k$, so $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is Noetherian; [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $X$ Noetherian. Choose a uniformizer $t$ of $A_0=\mathcal O_E$. By [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr], $A=A_0/(t)$ is a finite field; its characteristic is $\ell$, since $\ell$ belongs to the maximal ideal. By [sk-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x], the actual coefficient ring is $B=\mathcal O_{E,X}=\varprojlim_n(A_0/t^n)_X$. The bounded-constructible hypothesis on $K$ and $L$ [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible] means bounded cohomology constructible by general local finite presentations. Apply [lem-sfb-integral-lfp-constant-model-comparison] to each cohomology sheaf of $K$ and $L$: both complexes have bounded cohomology with finite constant local models. This invocation is the coefficient-specific bridge, not an identification by definition. Now apply implication (1) to (2) of [lem-sfb-integral-cohomological-adic-criterion], whose condition (1) explicitly uses finite constant scalar models. It gives local derived $(t)$-completeness of $K,L$, in the sense used by that criterion, and identifies $K_1=K\otimes_B^LA_X$, $L_1=L\otimes_B^LA_X$ with bounded finite-Tor-amplitude étale complexes with constructible finite-dimensional $A$-cohomology. Hence these reductions satisfy the explicit finite constant local model hypotheses of the finite-field child below.

source.place: Definition 6.5.1 and Proposition 6.8.11(3); Stacks Tag 09C0, proetale.tex, section-suitable-derived, for the adic criterion. The general-lfp to scalar-model comparison is the separate agent obligation cited in this step.

proof.text:
Set $H=R\mathcal Hom_B(K,L)$. Apply [lem-coef-integral-hom-reduction] to this $B$ and $n=1$, with its finite-field datum taken in the characteristic $p$ of $k$, so that its hypothesis $\ell\ne p$ is the one in force. Its statement applies to an arbitrary scheme and arbitrary ambient complexes; it does not impose a finite-ground-field or site-perfectness hypothesis. Its evaluation-defined comparison gives
$$H\otimes_B^LA_X\xrightarrow{\sim}R\mathcal Hom_{A_X}(K_1,L_1).$$
This is a comparison of the ambient internal Homs, not a new choice of Hom on a constructible subcategory. The completeness clause of that lemma is not used here: it concerns the derived-limit notion of completeness of its own definitions, whereas the criterion of step 1 uses local derived completeness; step 3 proves the latter for $H$ directly.

Apply [lem-sfb-finite-field-internal-hom-finiteness] to the finite field $A$ and to $K_1,L_1$ with their scalar-constant constructible cohomology established in step 1. By step 2, $H\otimes_B^LA_X$ is therefore bounded with finite constant local model cohomology. Apply [sk-thm-pe-constructible-comparison] on the Noetherian (hence qcqs) scheme $X$, with the discrete Noetherian field $A$, to obtain a bounded constructible étale complex $C$ whose pullback is this reduction. It has finite Tor amplitude: tensor of $A$-module sheaves is exact, as is checked locally by tensor of vector spaces and exact sheafification; consequently for a bounded complex its derived tensor with any degree-zero module sheaf has the same cohomological support bound. Next, $H$ is locally derived $(t)$-complete [def-weil-pbc-locally-derived-ringed-ideal-complete]. Let $U$ be an object of $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$, let $f\in(t)(U)$, and write $B_U$ for the restricted ring. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction], on $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ and on the slice site over $U$, together with the symmetry of the derived tensor product,
$$\begin{aligned}
R\mathcal Hom_{B_U}(B_U[1/f],H|_U)&\cong R\mathcal Hom_{B_U}(B_U[1/f],R\mathcal Hom_{B_U}(K|_U,L|_U))\\
&\cong R\mathcal Hom_{B_U}(K|_U\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{B_U}B_U[1/f],L|_U)\\
&\cong R\mathcal Hom_{B_U}(K|_U,R\mathcal Hom_{B_U}(B_U[1/f],L|_U))=0,
\end{aligned}$$
the last vanishing being the local derived completeness of $L$ from step 1. Together with this completeness of $H$, the étale complex $C$ verifies condition (2) of [lem-sfb-integral-cohomological-adic-criterion]. Its implication (2) to (1) gives bounded cohomology of $H$ with finite constant scalar local models. The reverse direction of [lem-sfb-integral-lfp-constant-model-comparison] makes these cohomology sheaves constructible in the general ring-object sense. Thus $H$ meets exactly the bounded-constructible predicate in the conclusion [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible].

source.place: Lemma 6.7.13 with R=A and m=0; Definition 6.5.1 and Proposition 6.8.11(3); Stacks Tag 09AI, proetale.tex, constructible comparison, and Tag 09C0, section-suitable-derived. Completeness of internal Hom: Bhatt–Scholze Lemma 6.7.13 proof (adjunction), via the ringed-site tensor–Hom adjunction and slice restriction.

proof.text: Use the ordinary unbounded layer-B derived category of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories] and the general local-finite-presentation predicate of [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible, def-sfb-constructible-module]. For the field-coefficient comparison lemmas below, their coefficient sheaves are $E_T=p_T^*\underline E$ and $\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell,T}=p_T^*\underline{\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell}$: [def-weil-pbc-condensed-e-module-category] defines $p_T^*=\pi_T^{-1}\circ a^*$, with $a^*$ the sheafified left Kan extension along $S\mapsto\operatorname{Spec}LC(S,\mathbf Z)$. This is term by term the construction in [sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point]. The ring $C(-,E)$ has exactly the sections of $\underline E$; the bounded-image ring $\underline\Omega$ has exactly the sections of the specified $\underline{\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell}$. Hence the comparison lemmas use $E_T$ and $\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell,T}$ themselves. The finite cokernel presentations coincide with [def-sfb-locally-finitely-presented].

source.place: Remark 6.8.15: ambient operations and coefficient passage; formal calculation from the cited adjunctions.

proof.text: For $E_X$ and $\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell,X}$ coefficients, apply respectively [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-lfp-local-triviality] and [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-qbar-lfp-local-triviality] to each locally closed stratum of each general-lfp constructible cohomology sheaf. Every such stratum is Noetherian because $X$ is Noetherian. By step 4 the coefficient sheaves and finite-presentation predicates agree with those in the two lemmas. They make the restriction pro-étale locally finite free, hence give finite constant local models with scalar modules $E^r$ or $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell^r$ in the sense of [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. Conversely a finite scalar presentation is a presentation over the coefficient sheaf by extending its matrix; extension of scalars preserves cokernels because it is a left adjoint [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]. Thus such scalar local models meet the general-lfp constructibility predicate. Boundedness is the same cohomological condition in both predicates.

source.place: Remark 6.8.15: ambient operations and coefficient passage; formal calculation from the cited adjunctions.

proof.text:
For any coefficient-ring map $R\to S$ on $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$, apply [lem-sfb-dc-hom-scalar-adjunction] in the ordinary unbounded derived categories. Write $K_S=S\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}K$ and $U$ for restriction. The lemma supplies the natural evaluation-normalized identification
$$U R\mathcal Hom_S(K_S,N)\simeq R\mathcal Hom_R(K,UN).$$
It also makes $U$ conservative. These conclusions will be used with $R=\mathcal O_{E,X}$, $S=E_X$, and with $R=E_X$, $S=F_X$ or $\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell,X}$. The lemma requires neither constructibility nor flatness. This cites the scalar-adjunction argument as a separate obligation rather than repeating it inline.

source.place: Remark 6.8.15 (ambient derived operations); auxiliary change-of-ring comparison, an agent formulation extracted from returned proof step 4, not a verbatim theorem of the source.

proof.text:
For integral $K_0,L_0$ bounded constructible in the general-lfp sense, [lem-sfb-integral-lfp-constant-model-comparison] applied to the cohomology of $K_0$ supplies the finite constant local models required by [lem-sfb-constructible-internal-hom-continuity]. This also applies to the integral representatives later furnished by the rationalization equivalence; no stronger hypothesis on those representatives is assumed. Take a bounded-below complex representative of $L_0$. By [sk-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x], $E_X=B[1/\ell]$ is the sequential colimit in sheaves of $B$-modules, equipped with its localization ring structure. Tensoring this module colimit with the representative gives the termwise colimit of $L_0\xrightarrow{\ell}L_0\xrightarrow{\ell}\cdots$. This system has a common lower bound. By [lem-sfb-constructible-internal-hom-continuity],
$$R\mathcal Hom_B(K_0,L_0)[1/\ell]
\simeq R\mathcal Hom_B(K_0,L_0[1/\ell]).$$
Here the left side is the same scalar localization of internal Hom. The module-object category is Grothendieck abelian by [lem-sfb-modobj-grothendieck], so filtered colimits are exact; tensoring with $B[1/\ell]$ is therefore exact, being the filtered colimit of tensoring with the free module $B$. Step 6 identifies the right side with the restriction of $R\mathcal Hom_{E_X}((K_0)_E,(L_0)_E)$. Hence the canonical evaluation-transpose map
$$E_X\otimes_B^L R\mathcal Hom_B(K_0,L_0)\longrightarrow R\mathcal Hom_{E_X}((K_0)_E,(L_0)_E)$$
is an isomorphism. Indeed its restriction is precisely the continuity map above; scalar multiplication by $\ell$ on the target is invertible, so the compatible maps from the stages define the displayed localized map.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.12 and Proposition 6.8.14(2); internal continuity is the explicitly named additional input.

proof.text: For arbitrary bounded constructible $E_X$-complexes $K,L$, apply [def-sfb-rationalization-equivalence] with the fixed prime $\ell$, finite subextension $E$ and its pulled-back coefficient rings. Its composite with localization is the restriction of $E_X\otimes_B^L-$ to bounded constructible complexes. The equivalence therefore gives integral bounded constructible representatives $K_0,L_0$ with $(K_0)_E\simeq K$ and $(L_0)_E\simeq L$: the standard localization has the objects of its source, and the equivalence is compatible with scalar extension. These representatives initially satisfy only the general-lfp predicate; step 7 applies to them because it explicitly invokes the integral comparison lemma. Step 3 makes $H_0=R\mathcal Hom_B(K_0,L_0)$ bounded constructible. By [lem-sfb-extend-scalars-bounded-constructible], $(H_0)_E$ is bounded constructible. The evaluation-compatible comparison proved in step 7 identifies it with $R\mathcal Hom_{E_X}(K,L)$. This proves the rational finite-extension case.

For bounded constructible $\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell,X}$-complexes $K,L$, choose a common finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ and bounded constructible $E_X$-complexes $K_E,L_E$ representing both, by [sk-thm-sfb-qlbar-two-colimit]. To obtain a common field from two initial fields, take their compositum and apply [lem-sfb-extend-subfield-constructible]. Put $H_E=R\mathcal Hom_{E_X}(K_E,L_E)$, bounded constructible by step 8. For every finite $F/E$, [det-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients-finite-free] identifies $F_X$ with a finite sum of $E_X$. Thus, after restriction, the canonical map
$$F_X\otimes_{E_X}^LH_E\longrightarrow R\mathcal Hom_{F_X}((K_E)_F,(L_E)_F)$$
is the finite-sum identification $H_E^{[F:E]}\simeq R\mathcal Hom_{E_X}(K_E,L_E^{[F:E]})$, using step 6. Its action on each basis summand is the identity followed by multiplication by that basis element. A different basis or the inclusion $F\subset F'$ gives a finite matrix of $E$-scalars; additivity and $E$-linearity of internal Hom make the same matrix act on both sides. Hence these are the evaluation-defined comparisons and commute with every field transition map, not just abstract isomorphisms.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14(1)–(2) and Remark 6.8.15; finite-free scalar calculation.

proof.text:
By [sk-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x], $\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell,X}=\varinjlim_F F_X$. Finite subextensions containing the chosen $E$ are cofinal: every $F_0$ is contained in $EF_0$, and any two such fields are contained in their compositum. This is a small filtered poset. Apply [lem-sfb-dc-hom-filtered-colimit] with $R=E_X$, $S_F=F_X$, $S=\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell,X}$, $K=K_E$, $L=L_E$. Its hypotheses hold: each $F_X$ is finite free by [det-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients-finite-free]; the module category is Grothendieck abelian by [lem-sfb-modobj-grothendieck], hence its filtered colimits are exact; $L_E$ has bounded-below cohomology; and step 5 gives the finite constant local models of $K_E$, so [lem-sfb-constructible-internal-hom-continuity] supplies exactly the lemma's common-lower-bound continuity hypothesis. The new comparison lemma gives the evaluation-transpose isomorphism
$$\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell,X}\otimes_{E_X}^{\mathbf L}H_E\xrightarrow{\sim}R\mathcal Hom_{\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell,X}}(K,L).$$
Its transition compatibility agrees with step 9. Finally [lem-sfb-extend-to-qlbar-constructible] makes the source bounded constructible, since $H_E$ is so by step 8. Thus the target internal Hom is bounded constructible.

Item statement: identical to the main-20261015 blueprint and not weakened. Proof sources checked: the unit, every cited node statement, and Bhatt–Scholze 3.4.11, 6.7.13, 6.8.10–6.8.15. No SGA in any step; the SGA 4½ string survives only in the imported source.external metadata. Steps 1–3 (integral case) hold: the lfp/scalar comparison on Noetherian X, adic criterion (1)=>(2), integral Hom reduction with n=1 and p=char k, the finite-field Hom node (hypotheses match), and the pro-étale constructible comparison. Finite Tor amplitude holds because every module over the field is flat. Local completeness is re-derived through the ringed internal-Hom restriction and currying. The step closes with (2)=>(1) and the lfp converse. Step 4 is a genuine elementary identification: p_T^* matches p_X^*, C(-,E) matches, and the bounded-image Omega matches Qlbar. Step 5 holds: the local-triviality lemmas give lfp => scalar models, and Ext preserves cokernels for the converse. Steps 6–10 (rational and Qlbar cases) hold: localization continuity with conservativity, the rationalization equivalence, two-colimit descent to a common E, the finite-free calculation, and the filtered lemma with every hypothesis checked. Both new nodes are true and are proper auxiliary lemmas. lem-sfb-dc-hom-scalar-adjunction follows from the Yoneda chain through the derived extension/restriction and tensor-Hom adjunctions, and U is conservative; I tested R=S, S=0 and Z->Z/2. lem-sfb-dc-hom-filtered-colimit is true under its continuity hypothesis, which is necessary: the counterexample F_p with an infinite direct sum fails without it. Both are self-contained statement-only nodes with searches recorded. My own DAG search found no duplicates and no restated parent clause. The route is fine, there is no cycle, and proof_deps equals the union of the steps' uses.
